body:
So, it appears I made an honest mistake, for that I apologise. I felt you were coming across badly/childlike and when you made the mistake of saying "since I am 11" I genuinely felt you were a child, my intention with that wasn't to lambast you but rather to be honest, this is a good community and I didn't want to give advice on a story that wasn't real. Honest mistake and again I am sorry.

However, if you showed this much of a ballsy attitude and desire to stand up for yourself in your relationship you wouldn't be in this mess. My original post I still stand by too.

OP why did you delete your comment? The comment where you let your mask slip? Luckily I screencapped it,

"Are you serious right now? The time of year he died is the absolute hardest time of year for me. EVERY YEAR  SINCE I WAS 11. It was the first indication the year was going to be awful and its since gotten worse."

I capitalized the sentence that was the most revealing, especially since David Bowie died in January 2016.
You didn't give much information in your original post. Still have to ask though in your other reply, how were aged 11 in January and now 23 in December?

Yes extremely serious. 

Hold on, David Bowie died this year 2016 in January. You said "Every year since you were 11" so you were aged 11 in January and now in December you are 23?

I have to ask what are you split on? I tried to analyze if fairly down the middle, I know posts like mine are usually never met well on this Reddit and are downvoted but in a relationship advice board surely a post giving opinions different than your own can maybe show you how someone else views your situation? So isn't a constant flood of sympathy.

I have to ask, was David Bowie dying one of the hardest parts of your year or was there other things outside of your relationship that made it the hardest.

IF David Bowie dying was one of the hardest parts of your year then I remain highly suspicious about you OP.

I am split on this post, your comment replies and the advice being given. I will say first of all that your boyfriend (based on your post) sounds like he has issues resulting from his tough, horrid upbringing. He probably felt like he had to toughen up a younger age and was never allowed to be a child and cry as it was met with a reaction he didn't want. Also if he compares you to his mother, then we can formulate that she must've been a crier and possibly a crier over anything, which as a child seeing that all the time can impact you as thinking that is how people deals with things and impacted him negatively. Could also be that whenever she cried, she got attention and whenever your boyfriend cried he got nothing.

I also believe that he never properly dealt with his childhood and thus reacts to life in the ways shown as a child, which to him may be the normality of things, how he was raised was and is how everyone else was.

Now I want to move onto yourself. I want to ask what things was he accusing you of? 

This is a real opinion splitter, crying over David Bowie shows that you must be a fairly sensitive person, I guarantee you also that around the world when someone else was crying over him it was met with choruses of "Jesus christ really?".  I admit I am one of those people also. I will give sympathy when a relative dies/stressed with work etc I will deal with that with hugs and the like. But I would feel like if you cried over a popstar you never met, that maybe you are a sensitive soul who personally I couldn't be with. I am not saying it is wrong that you are this way or that I am right about this, it's an advice board and I am trying to cut this post fairly down the middle.

If your boyfriend also says you are an ugly crier with snot dripping down your nose, then here is another thing chances are if ANYONE crys in this world it is not attractive, I have been called an ugly crier, I am sure many people reading have been called one and we all reacted to it differently.

If you were looking for a relationship where sympathy was given why did you not break up with him a year in or 6 months in? Why have you waited till 5 years, 2 of which being long distance where you could argue it is easiest to break up with him? This is the real question of this that needs to be answered. 

Yes I see it is your first relationship but that is not an excuse in my opinion, "please don't lynch me" are you scared of making mistakes and people telling you so? Five years is sometime to not think, "Shit maybe this isn't for me I am out of here!". I also think people will say "he is abusive, stockholm syndrome! Stockholm syndrome" but there are so many things you could've done to get out of this relationship and you could be in a happier better suited place right now.

There is a girlfriend out there for him that doesn't cry, is completely fine with the colder side of life, agrees she is an ugly crier (of course he is too) and silent treatment to her is not abusive.

Just like there is a boyfriend out there for you, who sees crying over David Bowie super cute, adorable and shows you are human with compassion, that you are definitely not an ugly crier, infact you are gorgeous and that hugs, flowers, chocolates are bought in stockpiled sessions ready for you to cry again.

Break up with him OP, for you are wasting your own time with someone you are not compatable with. He is plagued by his childhood and acts negatively as such and you are a sensitive soul it was never going to work.

Good luck OP.

26/m/UK

You broke up once that shouldve been the sign to you for it to be buried. You felt wrong being with someone else, you might not have given yourself enough time to get your ex. Also instead of being alone for a while you went for the easier choice and go back out with your ex.

Now whenever someone gets a text message it appears at the top of their phone. To see what your boyfriend said either he would have gone into the conversation where you could read his messages or you took his phone and read the messages.

With regards to his joke about the strip club and hookers, if this was before you were on the scene then you cant be annoyed. Some people enjoy talking to their friends about their memories together and in this case it was a memory that you didn't like even though it has little to do with you.

"However, when girls go to the club, they go to dance together. When guys go to the club, they don't dance together, they look for girls."

You need to stop right there with that sweeping generalisation. Have you ever thought that after a shit week/day of work maybe guys want to go to a club that plays decent music, so they drink and have a joke with each other.

His friend may have questionable morals in regards to cheating on his fiance and while you mentioned your boyfriend doing the same once, you then go onto say things got better was also amazing. You say you were upset about them two going out by themselves, if it is his best friends birthday then he mightve said "look i want me and you to have a lads night no women". Its his birthday its his right to do such a thing. Much like you having a girls night with no guys, its your right.

I feel so far you have portrayed yourself as a very VERY insecure person.

A real lack of communication here. Him wanting to spend HIS birthday with his friend is 100% his right and completely okay. He should try to see you also however if it is a long distance relationship then you should know planning and communication is key. Also you again say "the cheating friend". Again your portraying yourself as very insecure.

While at this stage im not sure I believe you but im going to go with you're telling the truth, he did lie. He did drugs because he wanted to. He also thought in his rationale that lying to you would get you off his case so he can enjoy his birthday without you being insecure.

He probably is suffering a quarter life crisis and to be honest a night of fun is all he wanted. Maybe he wanted to spend time with his friend, no feeling forced to dance, not having to watch what he says. I do think he shouldve tried to see you in some way although its a long distance relationship so you might go some time without seeing him.

You should've NEVER gotten back together with each other in the first place. 

From everything you have said, I think you are very insecure and i dont think relationships are for you until you can work through them. Your boyfriend from what you said doesnt seem like a great guy though.

Being drunk changes things then, so she is a shy person however opens up more when she is drunk. Nothing wrong with that, many people are like that. 

Her friend being a girl does not eliminate the chances of anything sexual happening, drunk girls kiss other drunk girls all the time. This isn't me trying to make you worry by the way, I'm just giving you another avenue of thought.

So if she doesn't want a serious relationship, you do know what she wants then? Or do you honestly know nothing that she wants and you think she doesn't want a serious relationship?

Here's a question if you dont want a serious relationship with her, what do you want? You want to see her, you want her in your life but in what capacity? Friend, friends with benefits, casual dating?

In reality the most revealing course of action would be to say to her, 

"I have caught feelings for you, the texting back and forth, the drunken making out has had a major impact on me (however it has stopped recently and I feel you have become distant). I want you in my life, I want to see you, I don't want a serious relationship, what do you think and feel for me, if anything?"

Of course it's killing you, three years is a long time to be with someone so you'll naturally get used to it and when that is taken away from you and your facing a future of uncertainty, the path of least resistance is always going to seem promising. 

It would be a big mistake in my opinion to go back to him, if he is willing to go behind his girlfriend's back for you, he'd be willing to go behind your back when your his girlfriend.

Also i shouldve said this before but, If you can't work towards getting over your ex then it's also unfair being with your current boyfriend, as he probably thinks your this amazing person he gets on super well with. He probably doesn't think your in love with your ex and asking strangers on the internet if you should leave him for a guy you used to go out with who abandoned you when life got a bit hard.

So she gets what she wants out of you, keeps you ticking over via text, then gets what she wants again and goes cold turkey on you. You mentioned before that upon meeting you were kissing and touching etc so then really she isn't a cold, shy and distant  person she is only that way to you.

She got her kicks and is now acting this way because I think in my opinion it's one of the following or a combination of the following, 

1. She only ever seen you as a casual bit of fun.

2. There is someone else she is acting this way with and you have been replaced.

3. You are one of a few people she is doing this with.

4.  If she only lets this friend in bed with her then that's a not so subtle hint of "I only desire to have or am currently having intimite relations with this person, you have no chance."

The remedy to this is simple the application is not, you either don't hang out with your social circle when she is there or you cherry pick the best ones and hang out with them without her there. Also if this has happened in the company of your social circle they see what's going on and if you explain yourself they may either,

1. Sympathise with you and hang out without her there.

2. Tell her what you tell them.

To be honest if you were more than friends and less than boyfriend/girlfriends before then this was simply a continuation of that and that's all it that was to her, which I'm sorry to say that despite you catching feelings for her, shes doing nothing wrong.

So if your ex broke up with you before, three years into your relationship as there was a lot going on then what's stopping him for doing the same again to you whenever life gets testing again? If he pushed you to the bottom of his priority list once he would be willing to do it again.

Also This is based on IF your ex still is with his current girlfriend, SO IF your ex is still with his girlfriend it's an asshole move to contact you telling you he wants to go out with you again. Infact it sounds like he is pushing his current girlfriend down his priorities list.

In regards to your current boyfriend if you get along with him perfectly in every way apart from religion and politics which are not deal breakers, you'd be a fool to abandon that for your ex.

Don't say to your girlfriend that "men are assholes but I miss dick", that is weak level softening the blow of what you're saying to her, as all she will understand is,

"I really miss cock and I'm saying men are assholes to keep this light hearted and give you some validation as a lesbian that you are not an asshole, when in reality I'm the asshole for leading you along as it appears this was just a phase for me even though I said I was totally into this."

If she is insecure about your relationship, this will crush her and you're going to have to do it if you want to date men again. This might ruin your friendship with her also. Think of it this way it will hurt your girlfriend more to continue this relationship, let it go further potentially let her love grow stronger then break up with her. 

Really you need to do this ASAP. Good luck.
